summary: A 1974 note sharing experience from implementing the Reconnection Protocol in the RSEXEC system, which let users on the ARPANET keep working across sites. It is a report of lessons learned.

eli5.summary: This is a note about what the builders learned while making it possible to reconnect to a lost session without starting over.

subtitle: Experience implementing the Telnet reconnection protocol to remove a middleman from the communication path

tldr.problem: When a user connected through an intermediary process to reach a remote host, the intermediary stayed in the communication path. Removing it required a complex protocol to safely hand off the connection.
tldr.mechanism: The Telnet reconnection protocol lets the intermediary send special commands to both the user and the remote host, requesting them to accept a direct connection and closing the intermediary's connections to both.
tldr.outcome: RFC 671 documents the TENEX implementation, showing how the protocol works in practice, the synchronization problems that arise, and lessons learned about error recovery and timing.

today: RFC 671 is Unknown status, a technical report on implementation lessons learned. Direct reconnection is rarely needed in modern systems where users typically establish independent connections, but the protocol concepts influenced later work on seamless network mobility and connection management.

sections.title: The Need for Reconnection
sections.content:
RFC 671 reports on implementation experience with the Telnet reconnection protocol in the Resource Sharing Executive (RSEXEC) system on BBN-TENEX. The reconnection protocol addresses a specific problem: when a user connects to a remote host through an intermediary process (such as a TIP user connecting through a service host), the intermediary becomes the middleman in every exchange. Reconnection allows the intermediary to step out of the communication path entirely, letting the user and remote host communicate directly.

This is useful for distributed computing scenarios where a job might span multiple specialized systems. As the user's work moves from one system to another, the communication paths can be rerouted without having to log out and log back in.
sections.eli5: Sometimes a person connects through a helper computer to reach the real computer they want. Reconnection lets the helper computer leave and the person connect directly.

sections.title: The Reconnection Protocol
sections.content:
The reconnection procedure works in several steps. First, the intermediary sends a special Telnet command (IAC DO RECONNECT) to both the user process and the remote server, asking if they are willing to reconnect. Both must agree before proceeding.

Next, the intermediary designates one party (the passive participant) to listen on a pair of sockets, and the other party (the active participant) to send connection requests (RFCs) to those sockets. The intermediary sends subnegotiation messages with the necessary host and socket information to both parties.

After both parties confirm they have the correct information and are ready, the intermediary closes its connections to both sides. The active participant sends RFCs, the passive participant receives them, and a direct connection is established. The intermediary is now completely out of the loop.
sections.eli5: The helper asks both sides: 'Can I connect you directly?' If both say yes, one listens and one calls, and the helper closes its own connections.

sections.title: Race Conditions and Error Recovery
sections.content:
A significant problem arises when both the user and remote host try to initiate reconnection at the same time (a race condition). When two IAC DO RECONNECT requests cross each other on the same Telnet connection, both ends detect this and must agree which reconnection attempt takes precedence.

The solution involves comparing a computed value based on the host address and receive socket number at each end. The end with the higher number wins; the other must reject the reconnection attempt so the winner's attempt can proceed. The loser can retry later.

Error recovery also addresses network delays and timing issues. The implementation must handle cases where the passive listener starts listening after the active participant has already sent RFCs (out of synchronization), or where timeouts occur. Two levels of error recovery are needed: one to retry failed connection attempts, and another to handle complete failure and possibly attempt alternative connections.
sections.eli5: If both sides try to reconnect at the same time, they use a tiebreaker based on their numbers. Also, if things don't line up timing-wise, the system tries again.
